title: The tray and the tooth, two vowels below, and the falling tone

slides.heading: Two letters, two vowels, and the tone that falls
body: Two consonants, another near-identical pair.
Two vowels, and the room under the floor.
The first tone that **falls**.

slides.heading: The shrine above the beach
body: Both low class, both at the harbour, both up at the shrine.
**Both breathe**, like the elephant. Everything before them hummed or stopped.
Two different places in your mouth: the lips, and the teeth.

slides.heading: Pen and paper first
body: Real paper, a real pen.
Today's pair is the closest yet. The hand separates them.
Out loud, both halves, every time.

slides.heading: The tray
body: Its name is the sound, then a word beginning with that sound.
The word means an **offering tray**.
A p with a puff behind it. The palm moves.

slides.heading: The woman who keeps the shrine
body: She has kept the shrine for forty years, and has not missed a morning.
Fresh flowers on the tray, incense lit, gone before the boats.
Nobody admits it matters. Nobody goes out if the tray is empty.

slides.heading: The sound she makes at the end of it
body: One short puff to put the flame out. Lips together, then open.
Three prongs, all three tips level. A tray set flat.
The head curls outside the left rim.

slides.heading: The tray's letter
body: Three prongs in a row, every tip level.
The head sits outside the rim, on the left.

slides.heading: Write it now
body: **Start at the head**, outside the rim on the left.
Three prongs, and all three tips stop **level**.
Leave it on the page. You will need it in two minutes.

slides.heading: The tooth
body: Its name is the sound, then a word beginning with that sound.
The word means a **tooth**.
And the sound is **made at the teeth**. The word tells you how to say it.

slides.heading: What is on the tray
body: A tooth the size of a hand, brought up in a net thirty years ago.
Nobody agrees what it came out of.
It has sat on the tray ever since, and every child tries to touch it.

slides.heading: Why it is that letter and not the other one
body: Same figure as the tray, with the last stroke grown taller.
One tooth standing up out of the row.
Nothing else separates the two letters.

slides.heading: The tooth's letter
body: The tray, with the final stroke risen above the rest.
Same head, same prongs. One of them outgrew the row.

slides.heading: Write it under the tray
body: Same head, same prongs. The last one keeps going.
Write it **directly under** the tray.
Compare your own two. That height is the whole difference.

slides.prompt: The two letters share a shape. Say the one difference, and which of them carries it.

answers: The final stroke rises above the rest.
The **tooth** has it. The tray keeps all three level.

slides.heading: The last room of the house
body: Back yard: written after. Roof: written above.
Underneath the floor is the **cellar**.
Two vowels today, and they arrive together.

slides.heading: The one who lives underneath
body: The name means **to carry**, or to hold something up.
A small hook, written underneath the consonant.
Where it is written is the only thing that puts him there.

slides.heading: And you have seen this trick before
body: Two of him: same sound, two lengths.
The long one is the same hook, drawn **deeper**.
**More stroke means longer.** Upstairs and down.

slides.heading: The short one, doing a job
body: The horse's letter, the small hook beneath, the horse's letter again.
**มุม** — a corner, or an angle.
Short: there and finished.

slides.heading: Write them both
body: Write both, one under the other. Compare the depth.
Always under a consonant, one you already know.
Say the **syllable** out loud, the sound the marks make together.

slides.heading: Read this one
body: The child's letter, with the deep hook beneath.
**Say it aloud before you turn it over.**

slides.heading: That one
body: **ดู** — to look, to watch.

slides.heading: Low class, stopped, on a long vowel
body: Low class, long vowel, dead ending: the pitch **falls**.
Short vowel in the same frame: it goes **high** instead.
The mark under the letter is where you read the length.

slides.heading: Two words you have been reading since lesson three
body: Both are low class, long vowel, dead ending.
Both fall, and both have since lesson three.
The rule gives you the tone before you have heard the word.

slides.prompt: Two words open on the tray's letter and both end dead. One falls and one goes high. Which is which, and what is the only thing separating them?

answers: Long vowel, dead ending, low class: **falls**.
Length decides it, and the depth of the hook shows the length.

slides.heading: One more to read
body: Tooth, curl above, snake closing it.
**Out loud before you turn it over.**

slides.heading: That one
body: **ฟัง** — to listen.

slides.heading: The opening band, finished
body: Twelve letters, seven vowels, four tone rules.
Three rooms of the vowels' house are open.
You can read a word you have never seen and know its tone.
